title: Add fast smoke-gates tier for batching/cache Optimize changes
author: Yara Haddad
body: Context: We’re adding mandatory quality guardrails before Optimize can apply cost-saving config changes (batching policy, prefix/KV caching). Full gate runs are comprehensive but can take 30–60 min and are expensive; teams need a faster precheck to catch obvious regressions and provide tight feedback loops during iteration. This PR introduces a new “smoke gates” tier that runs a small, high-signal prompt subset before scheduling full gates. Scope: smoke gates are enabled only for batching + caching config diffs (NOT quantization profile changes) and only in hosted/staging initially. Summary of changes: (1) Gate tier model: Introduces GateTier=SMOKE|FULL and stores tier on GateRun. A single Optimize recommendation/apply attempt now creates a GateRunGroup with an ordered plan (SMOKE -> FULL). (2) Prompt subset selection: Adds a new eval-harness request mode specifying prompt_set_id plus a “subset” selector. For smoke tier we use curated “gating_smoke_v1” subset (e.g., ~80 prompts) that is intentionally skewed toward known sensitivity cases for batching/caching (streaming boundaries, long-context prefix reuse, tool-call formatting). (3) Thresholds: Smoke tier uses stricter but simpler pass/fail logic to minimize false negatives: it blocks on (a) task_success drop beyond -0.5pp absolute OR (b) rubric_mean drop beyond -0.03, using a minimum sample size and a single rerun on variance spikes. Full tier keeps the v1 thresholds/variance model and is still required for any apply. (4) Scheduling + time bounds: Adds tier-specific SLAs and timeouts (smoke target <10 min, hard timeout 15 min; full unchanged). Implements a “fast-fail” policy: if smoke FAILS, we do not queue full. If smoke PASSES, we enqueue full automatically. (5) Fallback behavior: If smoke cannot produce a decision due to infra reasons (GPU capacity / eval-harness 5xx / timeout) we mark SMOKE=INCONCLUSIVE with reason_code and continue to FULL (so we don’t block rollout pipelines on smoke flakiness). If smoke is INCONCLUSIVE due to variance/flakiness (high flake_score or repeated inconclusive after rerun), we also proceed to FULL but emit a metric and annotate the Console summary to discourage relying on the smoke result. (6) Config + feature flags: Adds route-tier policy fields to gating policy config: smoke_enabled (default true for batching/cache), smoke_prompt_set=gating_smoke_v1, smoke_timeout_seconds, and a global kill-switch optimize.gates.smoke.disable for emergency rollback. Also adds allow_smoke_inconclusive_to_full (default true) to prevent accidental blocking during capacity events. (7) Observability: Emits gate_run_count and gate_run_latency_ms tagged by tier, plus smoke_inconclusive_total with reason_code. Adds a trace span “quality_gate.smoke” around the smoke execution path with eval_run_id linking to artifacts. (8) API behavior: The existing GateRun summary endpoint now returns “current_tier” and “plan” to support Console UX (Console work follows in ENG-3925). Apply remains blocked until FULL passes (or an override is granted) per PR-19531/PR-19537; smoke tier does not change enforcement semantics, only sequencing and time-to-signal. Test plan: Unit tests for plan construction (by config diff type), state machine transitions for SMOKE->FULL, and fallback handling; integration tests against eval-harness stub for timeout/5xx behavior; load test in staging to verify smoke tier reduces full-gate queue pressure on iteration workflows. Rollout plan: Enable smoke tier in staging immediately; enable for hosted production routes behind feature flag for internal accounts first, then expand during limited beta once we see stable inconclusive rate (<3%) and median smoke duration <8 min. Risks/notes: Primary risk is false positives due to subset skew; mitigated by allowing infra/variance inconclusive to proceed to full and by not allowing smoke to ever “greenlight” an apply. Coordination: Aligns with ENG-3923 and depends on the eval-harness trigger endpoint (PR-412) supporting subset selectors; if eval-harness does not recognize subset selector it returns 400 and we treat as INCONCLUSIVE(invalid_request) and proceed to FULL to avoid deadlocks. Related: PR-19502 (gate state machine), PR-19523 (wiring + retries), PR-19511 (config diff schema), PR-19531 (apply blocking).
commits: optimize/gates: add GateTier and gate plan sequencing
optimize/gates: implement smoke gate runner + decision logic
optimize/config: add smoke gate policy fields + feature flags
observability: emit tier-tagged metrics + tracing spans
tests: integration coverage for smoke timeout/5xx/inconclusive paths
review_conversation: Jonas Weber: Smoke subset looks reasonable. Two asks: (1) ensure smoke never becomes a substitute for full (i.e., apply should still require FULL=PASSED), and (2) please document the subset prompt_set_id and selection rationale somewhere discoverable. Also, what’s the planned rerun policy when flake_score is high?

Yara Haddad (author): Confirmed: apply still requires FULL pass; smoke is only a precheck and can only block early on FAIL. Added explicit guard in ApplyGateValidator requiring FULL=PASSED (and smoke result is ignored). For discoverability, I added gating_policy defaults + comments with prompt_set_id=gating_smoke_v1 and linked it to the internal prompt-set registry doc (will be expanded in docs PR). Rerun policy: 1 automatic rerun only when variance exceeds threshold OR flake_score>0.25; if still inconclusive we proceed to full and emit smoke_inconclusive_total{reason_code=flake}.

Selene Huang: On thresholds: -0.5pp task_success drop seems too sensitive for 80 prompts unless you’re doing a paired test / exact same sample. Are we comparing on identical prompt IDs? If yes, OK; if not, we need to avoid blocking on sampling noise.

Yara Haddad (author): Good catch—smoke uses a deterministic prompt list (fixed IDs) and always runs paired baseline vs candidate on the exact same prompts in the same job. Added a test asserting prompt IDs are stable (fetched by versioned subset). Also tightened the inconclusive logic: if we fail minimum sample or baseline missing, we mark INCONCLUSIVE instead of FAIL.

Sofia Ivanova: For batching policy diffs, we should be careful about changes that only affect scheduling but not outputs. Are we excluding ‘pure throughput knobs’ from smoke gating? Otherwise we’ll burn cycles on non-semantic changes.

Yara Haddad (author): We already do static diff classification via the config-diff schema; smoke/full gates only run for diffs that touch semantic-risk knobs (max_batch_tokens, continuous_batching_window_ms, prefix_cache_reuse_threshold, kv_cache_policy). Pure throughput knobs remain in validate-only path. Added an allowlist comment in GateDiffClassifier + a unit test.

Omar El-Sayed: Please ensure smoke timeout doesn’t deadlock the gate group (i.e., full should still run if smoke hits timeout). Also, we need a clear reason_code to distinguish timeouts from eval-harness errors.

Yara Haddad (author): Implemented SMOKE=INCONCLUSIVE with reason_code in {timeout, capacity, harness_5xx, invalid_request, flake, baseline_missing}. GateGroupPlanner treats all INCONCLUSIVE as proceed_to_full=true by default. Added integration test for timeout path.

Sean Gallagher: Observability: can you add a metric for “smoke saved full runs” (i.e., smoke FAILs that prevented full queueing) and ensure tags include route_id + config_type? We’ll want to alarm on rising inconclusive rate but not page from expected capacity events.

Yara Haddad (author): Added smoke_early_fail_total{config_type, model_family} and smoke_inconclusive_total{reason_code, config_type}. Route_id tagging is included where available but we keep it off high-cardinality metrics; route_id is present in structured logs and traces for drill-down. For alerting, I left a note in the metrics docstring to use reason_code filters to avoid paging on capacity.
Leila Farouk: Tests look good. One request: add an end-to-end test that asserts “smoke FAIL blocks and does not enqueue full”.
Benji Okafor: Approving after the guard on ApplyGateValidator. Please ensure policy defaults won’t enable smoke for quantization diffs.
Yara Haddad (author): Defaults explicitly set smoke_enabled=false for quantization config types; planner enforces that too. Added a regression test.
release_notes: Internal beta: Optimize quality gates now run a fast smoke tier for batching/prefix-cache changes before the full evaluation suite. Smoke failures block early; smoke inconclusive results proceed to full so apply behavior remains unchanged (still requires full pass/override).
